chunks: Aban, from Abdul Rahman ibn Abu Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
The woman marries whomever she wishes, if she is in control of her affairs; so if she wishes, she appoints a guardian.

key_terms.مَالِكَةً لِأَمْرِهَا: In control of her affairs / having autonomy

ai.seo_question: Does a woman need a guardian to marry according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi is central to the Shia juristic debate regarding the necessity of a guardian (wali) for a woman's marriage, asserting that a mature, independent woman (malakat li-amriha) can contract her own marriage without one. It highlights the flexibility within Shia fiqh, where the woman retains the agency to either act as her own wali or delegate this role to another, distinguishing between the right of autonomy and the formal requirement of guardianship in different legal schools.
